How this board works

Every price on this board is computed by our proprietary Dynasty Value Algorithm, built from deep analytics and market consensus. It weighs production, role and usage, age, and availability into a single value for every player, priced for this league’s scoring — the format is set in the League Format tool (Fantasy Tools menu). Where a player’s recent form runs ahead of his price — or behind it — he is flagged Leads algorithm / Lags algorithm. Tap “Why?” on any player for his season line, his usage, and his value history.

Risers & Fallers

How risers & fallers work

Every completed week is stored per player, so movement is a first-class signal, not an afterthought. A player’s role — his snap share and opportunities — often moves 1–2 weeks before his points do; where role and production disagree, the board flags a buy low (role rising, production lagging) or a sell high (production spiking on a flat role). Moves above are the latest weekly step at the format set in the League Format tool.

Rosters

How this works

A separate engine that answers a different question: not what your players are worth, but what your team does this season. Every player is re-priced as a rest-of-season projection — a redraft lens: this year’s remaining points. Each team’s best lineup is projected, then the rest of the season is simulated 10,000 times (the remaining regular-season weeks, plus the six-team playoffs). Nothing here feeds the dynasty values, the power score, or the trade calculator’s verdict — those stay exactly as they were. What it does feed is trade advice: Player Targets and the calculator show each deal’s title-odds swing next to its dynasty math, because a deal can be fair on value and still wrong for your window. Projections use this league’s actual scoring and do not move with the League format explorer.

How this works

The weekly question: who do I start Sunday? For the team you pick, this builds the optimal lineup for the current week from the weekly projections ESPN and Rotowire publish — printed exactly as the sources project them, never scaled up or down on this page. An injury designation rides as a tag on the player's name (Q, D, Out) for you to weigh yourself. A player on bye, or one the sources don't project at all, projects for zero and is auto-benched; a player listed Out who is nevertheless projected to play keeps his projection and is flagged a status conflict instead — a stale designation never erases a real projection. A player with no NFL team — unsigned, per the same live Sleeper players feed that carries the injury designations — projects for zero, is labeled Unsigned, and is excluded from the optimal lineup entirely, whatever his dynasty value says. A signed player outside the priced pool shows Unpriced rather than a fake zero: his projection is unknown, and he starts only when no priced option exists. Below it, the current real Sleeper matchup: both teams' optimal lineups, a win probability, and the decisions the game swings on. Same separation rule as everything else here — projections never touch dynasty values, and nothing in this tab moves a price on the board.

How the calculator works

Build a deal from any two rosters (or the free-agent pool). The verdict weighs trade value and team fit — each side's raw sum plus its value adjustment, so the side whose value sits concentrated in its best players gets credit for that concentration and one stud is not outweighed by a pile of lesser pieces — and whether the pieces fill a need, cost a starter, or fight a team's competitive window.

How Personalized Player Targets work

Pick a team and Player Targets works your window, not just your needs. A Win-Now ⏳ team only sees buys: picks, prospects and depth go out, production comes in — and every idea is checked against the rest-of-season projections, so a deal that lowers your optimal lineup’s projected points per week never appears, however the values balance. A Dynasty 👑 team sees buys too, but pickier ones: only clear upgrades, paid for with draft capital, so the young core stays intact. A Rebuilder 🔨 only sees sells: veteran starters converted into picks and young players, each one graded by the calculator’s fairness meter — value adjustment included — and only Fair or Close offers are shown. Crossroads 🔀 teams choose a direction: two labeled paths, Go Win-Now ⏳ and Go Rebuilder 🔨, each held to its own window’s rules.

Real Trades

Player prices are our algorithm's current values — what the pieces are worth today, next to what they fetched then. Pick prices use the mid slot on our pick ladder (2027–2029 rookie picks); picks from the 2025–26 classes — rookie picks dealt before their draft, and startup-draft picks in then-new leagues — are marked already drafted and shown unpriced: they really changed hands, but that draft is over and the pick itself no longer exists as a tradeable asset. A side with no players or picks listed received FAAB or considerations the feed doesn't itemize. Source: completed trades from public Sleeper leagues, collected Oct 18, 2026.

How waiver targets work

Every unrostered player in the snapshot, ranked for the team you pick — not by dynasty value, but by what he would do for that lineup. Each target is ranked by what he would add over the weakest starter he’d have to beat at his position, flex and superflex slots included — his projected points per week against that starter’s. Young players with a rising role get their own stash list — in dynasty, that’s usually where the wire pays. This league runs FAAB with a $300 budget. One honest note: with 32-man rosters, most weeks this wire is thin, and this page says so instead of dressing up a name.

League Format

A second QB starts in the SUPER_FLEX slot — QB2s hold real value instead of riding the bench. Turn it off and quarterbacks re-price for a 1-QB league, where only 12 QBs start and a replacement is always on the wire — so QB prices fall hard, and every other position barely moves.
How much each reception is worth. As it rises, wide receivers and tight ends gain a little; running back values barely move.
Extra points on every tight-end reception, on top of PPR. The bigger the premium, the more the elite tight ends separate from the rest of the position.

01 · The Ladder

Rookie pick ladder

Every pick priced by the Fantasy Forensics value algorithm and matched to the veteran it would take to buy it. An early 1st isn't an abstraction: it's a low-end fantasy starter. The ladder and the player board below run on the same scale, so every pick's price reads straight against the veterans beside it.

1.23×
Early 1st vs Mid 1st — the top tier of the round is worth about a quarter again the middle
1.33×
Early 1st vs Late 1st — draft position inside the round moves the price by about a third
1.27×
2027 Early 1st vs 2028 Early 1st — the one-year wait costs you about 21% of the value
PickValue Ovr rankWorth one veteranVet value (consensus)

Every slot on this ladder carries an Early / Mid / Late price — there is no single generic price for a pick, because where a pick lands inside its round is worth real value (see the tier gaps above). The prices are the Fantasy Forensics algorithm's, on the same scale as the main board, with future years discounted for the wait.

Picks appreciate into the draft

Value index of a future 1st across the 12 months before its draft (12 months out = 100). Modeled seasonal pattern: an in-season trough while veterans win games, then a steady climb through the combine to the April–May rookie-fever peak at the NFL Draft. Sell picks at the peak; buy them in October.

How to read the ladder

  • Early 1st ≈ rank ~17 veteran. A genuine starter — never throw one into a deal as a sweetener.
  • Mid 1st ≈ rank ~29. A solid WR2/RB2. Late 1st ≈ rank ~36, flex territory.
  • Early 2nd ≈ rank ~65. Bench-with-upside money. The drop from late 1st to early 2nd is only 1.26× — the softest round-boundary cliff on the board, and the classic trade-back target.
  • Round-over-round: early 2nd → early 3rd falls 1.56×. After the 3rd, picks flatten out (~1,260–1,970) and become fungible throw-ins.
  • Future years decay fast — a 2028 1st prices like a late 2027 1st; a 2029 1st like an early 2027 2nd.

03 · Post-Draft

Draft analyzer

Enter a completed rookie draft and get it graded: a letter grade per team, every pick scored against what that slot was worth on the ladder, steals and reaches flagged, and the league's winners and losers called out. Built for rookie drafts specifically — the tool the big sites never bothered to make.

Demo league loaded: Demo League. Draft order defaults to reverse standings and snakes each round — change any slot's team below.

The report code encodes the whole draft — send it to your league, they paste it below and the grades rebuild. Slot expectations follow the ladder's tier curve converted onto the algorithm's value scale (anchored where an early 1st equals our board's #25 player), normalized to the value actually available in this class — so a chalk draft grades around par and the grades separate on pick quality, not class hype.
04 · Live

Live draft room

A draft board that thinks while you pick: best-available recommendations tuned to the clock, tier-cliff alerts when a position is about to run dry, positional-run detection, and trade-back windows when your slot is worth more than anyone left on the board. Copy the room code and your co-owner follows the same board pick by pick — no other draft tool offers a shareable room.
